admission.contract: A halftone region segment is accepted as an MMR-coded payload and forwarded as a nonempty byte slice into halftone-region decoding.
limitations: This binds only the halftone-region MMR path described by the issue, not every MMR entrypoint in the project.
It does not prove the later multi-plane re-entry needed for the wrong-offset follow-on decode.

root.contract: One halftone MMR decode reports consuming more bytes than exist in its input slice.
limitations: This contract observes over-reporting at function exit, not the individual skipped refills that caused it.
It does not by itself identify which later caller use will consume the bad count.

target.contract: A later halftone MMR plane is initialized from the overreported offset, so the MMR prebuffer reads from a shifted pointer with wrapped remaining size.
target.predicate: root.report_consumed.hit && next_plane_call.hit && prefetch_byte.hit && next_plane_call.time > root.report_consumed.time && next_plane_call.consumed_bytes == root.report_consumed.reported && next_plane_call.consumed_bytes > next_plane_call.size && next_plane_call.remaining > next_plane_call.size && next_plane_call.next_data > next_plane_call.base_data + next_plane_call.size && prefetch_byte.data == next_plane_call.next_data && prefetch_byte.size == next_plane_call.remaining && prefetch_byte.i == 0
limitations: This requires a later GS plane decode, so it only applies when the halftone image has more than one bitplane.
The contract binds the wrong-slice prebuffer read; it does not prove how far later MMR decoding proceeds beyond that first mislocated read.
